subject: Clarify: what happens to user inputs vs model answers (default retention & residency)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@paylution.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: default retention for inputs vs model outputs + residency

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Paylution is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing payments assistant and we need to be clear about two things before we proceed:

1) By default, what does Redwood retain for hosted API requests? Do you keep full request payloads (user prompts), model outputs (generated answers), or just metadata?
2) For streaming or partial responses (prefixes while model is generating), are those fragments ever written to disk or logged?
3) Residency: can logs/retained items be restricted to EU-only (we need GDPR assurances)?

Could you point me to the default windows and the deletion flow? If there are contract options (shorter retention or guaranteed purge SLA) please flag those.

We’re on a tight timeline — any quick written summary would be helpful.

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of Security Operations
Paylution

--
Elena Torres
Paylution | security@paylution.com
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@paylution.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: default retention for inputs vs model outputs + residency

Elena — thanks for the thoughtful questions and for joining the demo. High level summary below; Marissa and Kim are copied for any compliance/engineering specifics. I also attached a short PDF summary.

Short answers (defaults):
- Request metadata (timestamps, route, token counts): retained for 90 days by default for operational troubleshooting and billing.
- Full request payloads (complete user prompts) and model outputs (generated text) are retained by default for 45 days for hosted customers; these are used for debugging and quality monitoring.
- Streaming fragments (prefixes sent during generation) are buffered in memory; we do not persist stream fragments to long-term storage by default — they may be cached in ephemeral storage for up to 7 days to support mid-session reconnects.

Residency options:
- For EU-residency customers we offer data residency where stored artifacts (requests/outputs/metadata) are pinned to EU regions. This is the default when you select EU during provisioning or as part of an enterprise contract.

Deletion flows / opt-outs:
- Self-serve: customers can enable an "opt-out of data retention for improvements" toggle in the Console; enabling this causes prompts/outputs to be excluded from persistent storage going forward.
- Contractual: for Enterprise/Private deployments we can add a deletion SLA (e.g., guaranteed purge of persisted artifacts within 72 hours of request) and narrower retention windows.

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf (high level table).

If you want, we can schedule a short call and Kim can walk through the retention architecture and purge playbook.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Quick Q: default retention for inputs vs model outputs + residency

Elena — adding a few clarifications on the technical and compliance side:

1) What we mean by "retained": there are three tiers we commonly reference in customer conversations —
   - Ephemeral runtime buffers: in-memory or short-lived caches used to support streaming and session reconnects. These are not written to durable object storage in the hosted control plane; retention is typically <= 7 days and mostly in-memory.
   - Operational logs & metadata: request IDs, timestamps, routing info, error codes, and token usage — retained 90 days by default to support billing, SLOs, and incident response.
   - Persistent artifacts (full prompts + model outputs + user-uploaded attachments): persisted to durable storage and by default kept 45 days for hosted customers unless you enable opt-out or contract a different term.

2) Derivatives and derivation rules:
   - Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranked indices, evaluation prompt sets we store for quality monitoring) are treated separately and we can scope them out of your tenancy on request.

3) Streaming specifics:
   - We do not write partial streaming frames to long-term logs. For reliability we may checkpoint short prefixes to ephemeral encrypted storage to support resume; those checkpoints expire under 7 days by default and are automatically garbage-collected.

4) Deletion mechanics & proof:
   - Self-serve deletion removes pointers and schedules object-level deletion. Actual physical deletion may incur short background TTL (object storage tombstone lifecycle) — typical completion is under 72 hours but depends on the selected storage backend.
   - For EU-residency customers we can provide a contract addendum with a 72-hour purge SLA and retention window adjustments (e.g., 7/30/90 day tiers depending on workload).

5) Evidence & SOC2:
   - We can provide SOC 2 artifact excerpts (see attached SOC2-excerpt.pdf) and a runbook describing the purge steps for legal/compliance review.

If you'd like, we’ll prepare a short redlined clause you can use in procurement that guarantees EU residency and a specific retention/purge SLA.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Product Privacy | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
